name: Entropy H(X)
type_signature: discrete RV X with pmf p → R_{≥0}
description: The expected value −Σ p(x) log p(x) of the self-information of a discrete random variable, measuring its average uncertainty in bits.
deps: discrete probability mass function, logarithm base 2

name: Joint entropy H(X,Y)
description: The entropy −ΣΣ p(x,y) log p(x,y) of a pair of random variables treated as a single vector-valued variable.
deps: joint probability mass function, entropy

name: Conditional entropy H(Y|X)
description: The expected entropy −ΣΣ p(x,y) log p(y|x) of Y averaged over the conditioning variable X.
deps: conditional pmf, joint pmf, entropy

name: Relative entropy (Kullback–Leibler divergence) D(p‖q)
description: The quantity Σ p(x) log(p(x)/q(x)) measuring the inefficiency, in bits, of assuming distribution q when the true distribution is p.
deps: two probability distributions on a common alphabet, convention 0 log(0/q)=0

name: Mutual information I(X;Y)
description: The relative entropy D(p(x,y)‖p(x)p(y)) between the joint distribution and the product of marginals, equal to H(X)−H(X|Y).
deps: joint and marginal distributions, relative entropy, entropy

name: Conditional mutual information I(X;Y|Z)
description: The expected reduction in uncertainty about X from knowing Y, given Z, equal to H(X|Z)−H(X|Y,Z).
deps: conditional entropy, mutual information

name: Mutual information–entropy relations
description: The identities I(X;Y)=H(X)−H(X|Y)=H(Y)−H(Y|X)=H(X)+H(Y)−H(X,Y) and I(X;X)=H(X).
deps: entropy, conditional entropy, joint entropy, mutual information

name: Chain rule for entropy
description: The joint entropy decomposes as H(X_1,...,X_n)=Σ_i H(X_i | X_{i−1},...,X_1).
deps: conditional entropy, joint entropy

name: Chain rule for mutual information
description: The mutual information decomposes as I(X_1,...,X_n; Y)=Σ_i I(X_i; Y | X_{i−1},...,X_1).
deps: conditional mutual information

name: Chain rule for relative entropy
description: The joint relative entropy decomposes as D(p(x,y)‖q(x,y))=D(p(x)‖q(x))+D(p(y|x)‖q(y|x)).
deps: relative entropy, conditional relative entropy

name: Jensen's inequality
description: For a convex function f and random variable X, E[f(X)] ≥ f(E[X]), with equality iff X is constant when f is strictly convex.
deps: convex function, expectation

name: Information inequality (Gibbs' inequality)
description: Relative entropy is nonnegative, D(p‖q) ≥ 0, with equality if and only if p=q.
deps: relative entropy, Jensen's inequality

name: Nonnegativity of mutual information
description: I(X;Y) ≥ 0 with equality if and only if X and Y are independent.
deps: information inequality, mutual information as relative entropy

name: Conditioning reduces entropy
description: H(X|Y) ≤ H(X), with equality iff X and Y are independent; conditioning never increases entropy on average.
deps: nonnegativity of mutual information

name: Uniform distribution maximizes entropy
description: For a finite alphabet of size m, H(X) ≤ log m with equality iff X is uniformly distributed.
deps: information inequality, relative entropy to uniform

name: Independence bound on entropy
description: H(X_1,...,X_n) ≤ Σ_i H(X_i), with equality iff the X_i are mutually independent.
deps: chain rule for entropy, conditioning reduces entropy

name: Log-sum inequality
description: For nonnegative a_i, b_i, Σ a_i log(a_i/b_i) ≥ (Σ a_i) log((Σ a_i)/(Σ b_i)), with equality iff a_i/b_i is constant.
deps: convexity of t log t, Jensen's inequality

name: Convexity of relative entropy
description: D(p‖q) is jointly convex in the pair (p,q).
deps: log-sum inequality

name: Concavity of entropy
description: H(p) is a concave function of the probability distribution p.
deps: relative entropy, convexity of relative entropy

name: Concavity/convexity of mutual information
description: For fixed p(y|x), I(X;Y) is concave in p(x); for fixed p(x), I(X;Y) is convex in p(y|x).
deps: mutual information, concavity of entropy, convexity of relative entropy

name: Data-processing inequality
description: If X→Y→Z form a Markov chain then I(X;Y) ≥ I(X;Z); no processing of Y can increase its information about X.
deps: Markov chain, chain rule for mutual information, nonnegativity of mutual information

name: Sufficient statistic
description: A statistic T(X) for a parameter family that retains all information about the parameter, characterized by θ→T(X)→X forming a Markov chain with I(θ;X)=I(θ;T(X)).
deps: data-processing inequality, mutual information, parametric family

name: Fano's inequality
description: For an estimate X̂ of X from Y with error probability P_e, H(P_e)+P_e log(|X|−1) ≥ H(X|Y), lower-bounding the error probability by the conditional entropy.
deps: conditional entropy, binary entropy function, estimator X→Y→X̂

name: L1 bound on entropy difference
description: If the L1 distance between two distributions p and q on an alphabet of size m is at most 1/2, then |H(p)−H(q)| ≤ −‖p−q‖_1 log(‖p−q‖_1/m).
deps: entropy, total variation distance

name: Asymptotic Equipartition Property (AEP)
description: For i.i.d. X_1,...,X_n ~ p, −(1/n) log p(X_1,...,X_n) → H(X) in probability.
deps: weak law of large numbers, i.i.d. source, entropy

name: Typical set A_ε^{(n)}
description: The set of sequences whose empirical entropy rate −(1/n) log p(x^n) is within ε of H(X), i.e. whose probability is near 2^{−nH}.
deps: AEP, entropy

name: Properties of the typical set
description: The typical set has probability near 1, has at most 2^{n(H+ε)} elements, at least (1−ε)2^{n(H−ε)} elements, and each member has probability near 2^{−nH}.
deps: typical set, AEP

name: AEP-based source coding bound
description: i.i.d. sequences can be encoded with about nH(X) bits using roughly n(H+ε) bits per typical sequence and a negligible-probability overflow code.
deps: typical set properties, source coding

name: Smallest high-probability set B_δ^{(n)}
description: A minimum-cardinality set carrying probability at least 1−δ, whose size to first order in the exponent equals that of the typical set (≈ 2^{nH}).
deps: typical set, AEP

name: Entropy rate H(𝒳)
description: The per-symbol limit H(𝒳)=lim_{n→∞} (1/n) H(X_1,...,X_n) of the entropy of a stationary stochastic process.
deps: stationary process, joint entropy, limit

name: Equivalence of entropy-rate definitions
description: For a stationary process the limit H'=lim H(X_n | X_{n−1},...,X_1) exists and equals the entropy rate H(𝒳).
deps: stationarity, Cesàro mean, conditioning reduces entropy

name: Markov chain (stochastic process)
type_signature: sequence of RVs with transition matrix P
description: A discrete-time process in which the conditional distribution of the next state depends only on the current state.
deps: conditional distribution, transition probability matrix

name: Stationary distribution
description: A probability vector invariant under the transition matrix of a Markov chain, fixed by μ_j=Σ_i μ_i P_{ij}.
deps: Markov chain, transition matrix

name: Entropy rate of a Markov chain
description: For a stationary Markov chain with stationary distribution μ and transition matrix P, the entropy rate is H(𝒳)=−Σ_{ij} μ_i P_{ij} log P_{ij}.
deps: entropy rate, stationary distribution, Markov chain

name: Entropy rate of a hidden Markov / functions of Markov chains
description: For a function Y_i=φ(X_i) of a stationary Markov chain, the entropy rate is squeezed between H(Y_n|Y_{n−1},...,Y_1,X_1) and H(Y_n|Y_{n−1},...,Y_1), both converging to it.
deps: entropy rate, Markov chain, functions of a process

name: Markov chains and the second law
description: For a Markov chain, relative entropy D(μ_n‖μ'_n) to any other distribution evolving under the same transition decreases with time, and H(X_n) increases toward stationarity for a doubly stochastic chain.
deps: relative entropy, Markov chain, data-processing

name: Kraft inequality
description: A prefix (instantaneous) code over a D-ary alphabet with codeword lengths l_i exists if and only if Σ_i D^{−l_i} ≤ 1.
deps: prefix code, D-ary alphabet, codeword lengths

name: Prefix (instantaneous) code
description: A code in which no codeword is a prefix of any other, so each symbol is decodable as soon as its codeword ends.
deps: variable-length code, codeword alphabet

name: Uniquely decodable code
description: A code whose extension to sequences is nonsingular, so every encoded string has at most one source interpretation.
deps: variable-length code, code extension

name: Kraft–McMillan inequality
description: The codeword lengths of any uniquely decodable code satisfy Σ D^{−l_i} ≤ 1, so uniquely decodable codes offer no better lengths than prefix codes.
deps: uniquely decodable code, Kraft inequality

name: Entropy bound on expected codeword length
description: The expected length L of any prefix D-ary code satisfies L ≥ H_D(X), with equality iff the lengths are l_i=−log_D p_i.
deps: Kraft inequality, relative entropy, optimal code

name: Shannon code lengths
description: The codeword-length assignment l_i=⌈log(1/p_i)⌉ which satisfies Kraft and achieves expected length within one bit of entropy.
deps: Kraft inequality, entropy bound on codeword length

name: Optimal code length bound (H ≤ L < H+1)
description: The minimum expected length L* of a prefix code satisfies H_D(X) ≤ L* < H_D(X)+1, and block coding drives the per-symbol length to the entropy rate.
deps: Shannon code, entropy bound, block coding

name: Penalty for using the wrong code
description: Using a code optimal for q to encode a source p costs an extra D(p‖q) bits per symbol over the entropy, i.e. expected length is between H(p)+D(p‖q) and H(p)+D(p‖q)+1.
deps: relative entropy, Shannon code, entropy

name: Huffman coding
description: A bottom-up algorithm that builds an optimal prefix code by repeatedly merging the least probable symbols into a combined symbol.
deps: prefix code, Kraft inequality, expected length minimization

name: Optimality of Huffman codes
description: The Huffman code achieves the minimum expected codeword length over all prefix (hence all uniquely decodable) codes for a given source.
deps: Huffman coding, properties of optimal codes, Kraft–McMillan

name: Shannon–Fano–Elias coding
description: A coding scheme using the rounded cumulative distribution function F̄(x) truncated to ⌈log(1/p(x))⌉+1 bits to assign prefix-free codewords.
deps: cumulative distribution function, prefix code, Kraft inequality

name: Arithmetic coding
description: A coding technique that represents an entire sequence by an interval of the unit line determined by cumulative probabilities, encoded by a single number.
deps: Shannon–Fano–Elias coding, cumulative distribution, sequential model

name: Competitive optimality of Shannon code
description: For Shannon code lengths l(x), no other uniquely decodable code l'(x) can satisfy l'(x) < l(x)−c with probability exceeding 2^{−c+1}; the Shannon code is essentially uncrushable.
deps: Shannon code, Kraft inequality, dyadic distributions

name: Horse race / gambling model
type_signature: outcomes with probabilities p_i and odds o_i
description: A repeated investment model in which a gambler distributes wealth across m outcomes with win probabilities p_i and payoff odds o_i.
deps: probability distribution, betting proportions, odds

name: Doubling rate W(b,p)
description: The expected logarithmic growth rate W(b,p)=Σ p_i log(b_i o_i) of wealth per race under bet allocation b.
deps: horse race, expected log wealth

name: Kelly (proportional) gambling optimality
description: The doubling rate is maximized by proportional betting b_i=p_i, yielding optimal doubling rate W*(p)=Σ p_i log o_i − H(p).
deps: doubling rate, Jensen / Kuhn–Tucker, horse race

name: Conservation theorem (gambling)
description: For uniform fair odds o_i=m, the sum of the doubling rate and the entropy is constant: W*(p)+H(p)=log m.
deps: Kelly optimality, entropy, fair odds

name: Value of side information in gambling
description: The increase ΔW in doubling rate due to side information Y equals the mutual information I(X;Y) between the horse race outcome and the side information.
deps: doubling rate, mutual information, Kelly betting

name: Doubling rate of dependent horse races
description: For a sequence of races, the growth-rate-optimal wealth grows as 2^{nW*} where the per-race doubling rate relates to the entropy rate via W*=Σ log o − H(𝒳) for fair uniform odds.
deps: doubling rate, entropy rate, gambling estimate of entropy

name: Entropy of English
description: The estimated entropy rate of English (about 1.3 bits/letter) obtained via models and Shannon's guessing/gambling estimation games.
deps: entropy rate, stochastic model of language, gambling estimate

name: Discrete memoryless channel (DMC)
type_signature: (input alphabet X, transition p(y|x), output alphabet Y)
description: A channel specified by a conditional distribution p(y|x) that acts independently on each transmitted symbol.
deps: transition probability, input/output alphabets, memorylessness

name: Channel capacity C
description: The maximum mutual information C=max_{p(x)} I(X;Y) over input distributions, the information capacity of the channel.
deps: discrete memoryless channel, mutual information, maximization over input pmf

name: Binary symmetric channel (BSC)
description: A binary-input binary-output channel that flips each bit independently with probability p, having capacity 1−H(p).
deps: discrete memoryless channel, binary entropy function

name: Binary erasure channel (BEC)
description: A binary-input channel that erases each symbol with probability α and otherwise transmits it correctly, having capacity 1−α.
deps: discrete memoryless channel, erasure symbol

name: Symmetric and weakly symmetric channels
type_signature: channel with permuted rows/columns of transition matrix
description: A channel whose transition-matrix rows are permutations of one another (and columns sums equal), for which capacity equals log|Y|−H(row) achieved by the uniform input.
deps: discrete memoryless channel, channel capacity, uniform input

name: Jointly typical set A_ε^{(n)}
description: The set of pairs (x^n,y^n) that are individually typical and whose joint empirical entropy is near H(X,Y).
deps: typical set, joint entropy, AEP

name: Joint AEP
description: Jointly typical pairs have probability near 1, number about 2^{nH(X,Y)}, and an independently drawn pair is jointly typical with probability about 2^{−nI(X;Y)}.
deps: jointly typical set, AEP, mutual information

name: Channel code (M, n)
description: An encoding of M messages into length-n channel inputs together with a decoding rule, with rate R=(log M)/n bits per channel use.
deps: discrete memoryless channel, encoder, decoder, rate

name: Channel coding theorem (achievability)
description: For any rate R < C there exist codes with maximal error probability tending to 0; all rates below capacity are achievable.
deps: channel capacity, joint AEP, random coding, jointly typical decoding

name: Converse to the channel coding theorem
description: Any sequence of (2^{nR},n) codes with error probability tending to 0 must have R ≤ C; capacity is the supremum of achievable rates.
deps: Fano's inequality, data-processing inequality, channel capacity

name: Random coding argument
description: A proof method that generates a codebook at random from p(x), bounds the expected error probability, and concludes a good code exists.
deps: jointly typical decoding, joint AEP, expectation argument

name: Jointly typical decoding
description: A decoder that declares the unique codeword jointly typical with the received sequence, erring only on atypicality or collision.
deps: jointly typical set, joint AEP

name: Feedback capacity theorem
description: Feedback does not increase the capacity of a discrete memoryless channel: C_FB=C.
deps: channel capacity, converse, data-processing

name: Source–channel separation theorem
description: A source of entropy rate H can be transmitted reliably over a channel of capacity C iff H < C, and separate optimal source and channel coding is asymptotically optimal.
deps: channel coding theorem, AEP source coding, Fano's inequality

name: Zero-error capacity
description: The largest rate at which messages can be sent over a channel with exactly zero probability of error, related to the independence number of the channel's confusability graph.
deps: discrete memoryless channel, combinatorial confusability graph

name: Hamming code
description: A linear block code with minimum distance 3 capable of correcting any single bit error, illustrating explicit error-correcting construction.
deps: channel code, parity-check matrix, minimum distance

name: Differential entropy h(X)
type_signature: continuous RV with density f → R ∪ {±∞}
description: The quantity h(X)=−∫ f(x) log f(x) dx, the continuous analogue of entropy for a random variable with density f.
deps: probability density function, integral, logarithm

name: Differential entropy of uniform and Gaussian
description: The uniform on [0,a] has differential entropy log a, and the N(0,σ²) Gaussian has differential entropy (1/2) log(2πeσ²).
deps: differential entropy, uniform/normal density

name: AEP for differential entropy
description: For i.i.d. continuous X_i with density f, −(1/n) log f(X^n) → h(X), and the typical set has volume about 2^{nh(X)}.
deps: AEP, differential entropy, weak law of large numbers

name: Relation of differential to discrete entropy
description: The entropy of an n-bit quantization of a continuous X satisfies H(X^{Δ}) ≈ h(X)+n, so differential entropy is discrete entropy minus the log of the quantization step.
deps: differential entropy, quantization, Riemann integral

name: Joint and conditional differential entropy
description: The differential entropies h(X,Y)=−∫ f log f and h(X|Y)=h(X,Y)−h(Y) defined for jointly continuous variables.
deps: differential entropy, joint density

name: Continuous relative entropy and mutual information
description: The relative entropy D(f‖g)=∫ f log(f/g) and mutual information I(X;Y)=h(X)−h(X|Y) for continuous variables, both nonnegative.
deps: differential entropy, density, information inequality

name: Entropy of the multivariate Gaussian
description: A multivariate normal with covariance K has differential entropy (1/2) log((2πe)^n |K|).
deps: differential entropy, covariance matrix, determinant

name: Gaussian maximizes differential entropy
description: Among all densities with a given covariance K, the multivariate Gaussian uniquely maximizes differential entropy.
deps: differential entropy, relative entropy to Gaussian, covariance constraint

name: Hadamard's inequality (via entropy)
description: For a positive-definite covariance matrix K, |K| ≤ Π K_{ii}, derived from the independence bound on differential entropy.
deps: multivariate Gaussian entropy, independence bound on entropy

name: Gaussian channel
description: A continuous channel adding independent Gaussian noise of power N to the input, typically under an input power constraint E[X²] ≤ P.
deps: continuous channel, Gaussian noise, power constraint

name: Capacity of the Gaussian channel
description: The power-constrained Gaussian channel has capacity C=(1/2) log(1+P/N) bits per transmission, achieved by Gaussian inputs.
deps: Gaussian channel, channel capacity, Gaussian maximizes entropy

name: Sphere-packing argument
function_signature: (power P, noise N, n) → (number of distinguishable codewords)
description: A geometric heuristic counting how many noise spheres of radius √(nN) pack into a signal sphere of radius √(n(P+N)), yielding 2^{nC} codewords.
deps: Gaussian channel, volume of n-sphere, capacity

name: Capacity of the band-limited Gaussian channel
description: A band-limited channel of bandwidth W with power P and noise spectral density N_0/2 has capacity W log(1+P/(N_0 W)) bits per second.
deps: Gaussian channel capacity, Nyquist sampling theorem, bandwidth

name: Parallel Gaussian channels capacity
description: For k independent Gaussian channels under a total power constraint, capacity is Σ (1/2) log(1+P_i/N_i) maximized over a power allocation summing to P.
deps: Gaussian channel capacity, Lagrange optimization, power allocation

name: Water-filling power allocation
function_signature: (noise levels N_i, total power P) → (optimal powers P_i)
description: The optimal allocation P_i=(ν−N_i)^+ that pours power into the lowest-noise channels up to a common water level ν.
deps: parallel Gaussian channels, Karush–Kuhn–Tucker conditions

name: Capacity with colored Gaussian noise
description: For a Gaussian channel with non-white noise of covariance K_Z, capacity is obtained by water-filling over the eigenvalues of the noise covariance under a power constraint.
deps: parallel Gaussian channels, water-filling, eigendecomposition of covariance

name: Gaussian channel with feedback
description: For the colored Gaussian channel feedback increases capacity by at most half a bit and at most a factor of two; for the memoryless (white) Gaussian channel feedback does not increase capacity.
deps: Gaussian channel capacity, feedback, covariance optimization

name: Rate-distortion function R(D)
type_signature: (source p(x), distortion d, level D) → R_{≥0}
description: The minimum mutual information R(D)=min_{p(x̂|x): E d(X,X̂) ≤ D} I(X;X̂) needed to describe a source within average distortion D.
deps: distortion measure, mutual information, source distribution

name: Distortion measure d(x,x̂)
description: A nonnegative function quantifying the cost of representing source symbol x by reconstruction x̂ (e.g. Hamming or squared-error).
deps: source and reconstruction alphabets

name: Rate-distortion theorem
description: The operational rate-distortion function (minimum rate for distortion ≤ D) equals the information rate-distortion function R(D)=min I(X;X̂).
deps: rate-distortion function, joint AEP, random coding, converse

name: Rate-distortion of a Bernoulli source
description: A Bernoulli(p) source under Hamming distortion has R(D)=H(p)−H(D) for 0 ≤ D ≤ min(p,1−p) and 0 beyond.
deps: rate-distortion function, binary entropy, Hamming distortion

name: Rate-distortion of a Gaussian source
description: A N(0,σ²) source under squared-error distortion has R(D)=(1/2) log(σ²/D) for D ≤ σ² and 0 for D ≥ σ².
deps: rate-distortion function, differential entropy, squared-error distortion

name: Rate-distortion for parallel Gaussian sources (reverse water-filling)
description: For independent Gaussian sources under total squared-error distortion, the optimal distortion allocation D_i=min(λ,σ_i²) gives reverse water-filling, allocating no rate to low-variance components.
deps: Gaussian rate-distortion, Lagrange optimization, water-filling

name: Convexity and monotonicity of R(D)
description: The rate-distortion function R(D) is a nonincreasing convex function of the distortion level D.
deps: rate-distortion function, convexity of mutual information

name: Blahut–Arimoto algorithm
description: An alternating-minimization iteration that computes channel capacity or the rate-distortion function by treating them as a double minimization over two distributions.
deps: channel capacity, rate-distortion function, alternating optimization, relative entropy

name: Capacity / R(D) as double optimization
description: Both channel capacity and the rate-distortion function can be written as a minimization of relative entropy over two distributions, justifying the Blahut–Arimoto alternating scheme.
deps: relative entropy, channel capacity, rate-distortion function

name: Strong typicality / method of types (preview)
description: Sequences classified by their empirical type (histogram) so that the probability of a type and the number of sequences of a type are governed by entropy and relative entropy exponents.
deps: empirical distribution, entropy, relative entropy

name: Binary entropy function H(p)
description: The entropy −p log p −(1−p) log(1−p) of a Bernoulli(p) variable, a concave function peaking at p=1/2.
deps: entropy, Bernoulli distribution
